evidence_type: Single runtime verification result; not a benchmark
provenance: Sanitized summary of captured ROS target, TF, joint-state feedback, planned path and node result logs; visual confirmation supplied separately by the user.

target_definition.description: Freshly queried current pose plus 0.03 metres along planning-frame X; Y, Z and current orientation preserved.

visible_motion.confirmation_source: User observation in the Isaac Sim viewer

runtime_integration_findings: ROS processes ran as ubuntu, matching the running Isaac process, to resolve Fast DDS shared-memory permission issues in this environment.
The unchanged node was supplied the live MoveIt robot description, semantic model and kinematics parameters, with use_sim_time enabled.
measurement_notes: Client-side planning latency measures plan(plan); execution latency measures execute(plan), using the existing steady-clock instrumentation.
Total latency includes intervening logging and handling, excluding target validation and TF transformation.
The pose target is not a straight-line Cartesian path constraint.
Joint feedback and the observed endpoint corroborate motion; controller success does not imply zero tracking error.
This single run does not establish repeatability, latency distributions or performance guarantees.
The supplied target was already in the planning frame; this run did not exercise cross-frame target transformation.
